Trump says victory over Iran 'at hand', stress that Tehran will 'never have a nuclear weapon'
articles.summary:
Trump says victory over Iran 'at hand', stress that Tehran will 'never have a nuclear weapon'

US President Donald Trump said that Washington will be victorious over Iran "whenever" he wants it to happen. 

"We have victory at hand (in Iran). It's going to be whenever, sort of, whatever I want it to be. To be honest, and we're trying to be nice, we're giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives. But I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," he said during Thanksgiving calls with US service members.

Trump also praised US forces for their role in the war on Iran, adding that they would never allow Tehran to have nuclear arms. 

"Each of you is playing an essential role to protect not only our country today but future generations of Americans by ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. They will never have a nuclear weapon. That I can tell you."

University of Michigan faculty vote in support of pro-Palestine students facing charges
articles.summary:
University of Michigan faculty vote in support of pro-Palestine students facing charges

Nearly 60 percent of voting faculty members at the University of Michigan have backed a resolution in support of a dozen former students and staff who are now facing federal criminal charges for their participation in the 2024 anti-war encampments for Gaza. 

The move is symbolic but also an indication of where much of the teaching staff stands. 

On 12 November, after 2,425 members of the Faculty Senate voted on a motion stating that the Department of Justice's indictment "is part of a broader attack on both Palestine solidarity and labor unions in the United States", results showed 58.2% expressed support. 

That's more than 1,000 professors, lecturers, clinicians, and other University of Michigan employees. 

Read more: University of Michigan faculty vote in support of pro-Palestine students facing charges

articles.title: South Korea assures Iran that it has no plans of participating in the war
articles.summary:
South Korea assures Iran that it has no plans of participating in the war

During a phone call, South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun assured Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi that Seoul has "no intention of intervening in or participating in the war".

The two exchanged views on their bilateral relations and the situation in the Middle East, discussing recent diplomatic efforts and initiatives to maintain peace and stability in the region.

According to a post on X by the Iranian Embassy in Seoul, Araghchi expressed concern regarding the "presence of any foreign military forces in the region, stressing that rather than contributing to peace and security, such a presence would heighten tensions and expand the scope of the conflict".

"Foreign Minister Cho reaffirmed South Korea’s support for peace and stability in the region, assuring Foreign Minister Araghchi that South Korea has no intention of intervening in or participating in the war and no plans to deploy troops to the region," the post added.

articles.summary: Israeli police clashed with ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters, known as Haredim, during a demonstration against mandatory military service at the Bar-Ilan Junction in West Jerusalem on Thursday, Anadolu Agency reports. Mounted police and officers moved in to disperse protesters attempting to block traffic, using force against demonstrators. They have traditionally refused military service, saying they need to devote themselves to studying the Torah and that integration into secular society threatens their religious identity. articles.title: Iran says Qatari, Pakistani mediation in talks with US continues
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Thursday that mediation efforts by Qatar and Pakistan in negotiations between Tehran and Washington are continuing. Speaking to Iranian state television, Araghchi said Qatari and Pakistani mediators remain engaged and are regularly conveying ideas and proposals between the two sides. He said, however, that Iran’s Foreign Ministry is prioritizing efforts to strengthen the country’s economic resilience against sanctions rather than focusing solely on negotiations. Tehran is working through various channels to meet its needs and counter attempts to impose an economic blockade and sanctions, he added. “We are examining ideas that could open new paths, but we insist on implementing our demands related to reopening the Strait of Hormuz,” Araghchi said.
